§6Fission Products: I-131, Cs-137, Sr-90, Po-210

§aIsotopes from nuclear waste. Some are trash, some power your RTGs for years.

§6Iodine-131 (Radiodine)§f:
Extremely radioactive, pyrophoric. ~6.3% of Short-Lived Nuclear Waste. No current uses.

§6Caesium-137§f (§e20 RAD/s§f):
~9% of short-lived waste. Planned for salted nukes, not yet implemented.

§6Strontium-90§f (§e15 RAD/s§f):
~5.5% of short-lived waste. Makes §bRTG pellets§f at §e15 power/tick§f, lasting §e208.8M ticks§f (~4 real months). Decays to zirconium.

§6Polonium-210§f (§e75 RAD/s§f, pyrophoric):
From recycling Ra226Be sources or cyclotron. Makes §bPo210Be neutron sources§f (better than Ra226Be), §bRTG pellets§f at §e50 power/tick§f, and §bSelf-Charging Batteries§f at §e1.25 kHE/t§f.

§ePS:§f Sr-90 and Po-210 are the money isotopes. Set up a SILEX to process short-lived waste and extract them. Iodine and caesium are just noise for now.
